question: What is the cost price of an article which is sold for ₹1,566 with 8% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the profit is 8%, the Selling Price (SP) is 108% of the Cost Price (CP).

108% → ₹1,566

1% → 1,566 ÷ 108 = 14.5

100% → 14.5 × 100 = 1450

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,450.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,566

Profit Percentage = 8%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit %)

 
• 
 

 +8% Profit
 
 CP (100%)
 ?
 
 SP (108%)
 ₹1,566

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (1566 × 100) ÷ (100 + 8)

⇒ CP = (1566 × 100) ÷ 108

⇒ CP = 14.5 × 100

⇒ CP = 1450

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,450.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When an article is sold at a loss, the Cost Price is calculated as: CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss %).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price is calculated as SP = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.
